name: Battle of Boyacá

phases.title: The vanguards meet at Casa de Teja
phases.text: The Royalist vanguard had stopped near Casa de Teja to rest. Patriot skirmishers met it, and Santander ordered the Cazadores Battalion to attack the Royalists there.

phases.title: The Royalist vanguard falls back over the bridge
phases.text: The Royalist vanguard crossed the bridge over the Teatinos River and took defensive positions there. Santander's full vanguard reached Casa de Teja, and he sent Bejar down the river to cross it and attack the Royalists from the rear.

phases.title: The Royalist rearguard is cut off
phases.text: The Royalist rearguard was still several kilometres behind, and Anzoátegui blocked the way between it and the vanguard. Outnumbered, it retreated to a small hill and formed with its guns in the centre, infantry beside them and cavalry on the wings.

phases.title: Flank attack ordered on the Royalist rearguard
phases.text: Anzoátegui ordered a flank attack on the Royalist rearguard. Barcelona and Bravos de Paez were to attack on the right side and the British Legion and Rifles on the left, and the two groups moved up to the Royalist line.

phases.title: Sandes charges the Royalist guns
phases.text: Arthur Sandes, commander of the Rifles, charged the Royalist artillery. The charge disrupted the arming of the three guns, which had been carried unassembled. Only one was put together, and it fired three shots before its carriage broke.

phases.title: Patriot lancers drive back the Royalist dragoons
phases.text: Bolívar ordered lancers to attack the centre of the Royalist infantry. The 3rd and 5th companies of the Granadan Dragoons charged the patriot cavalry, which turned to face them, and the dragoons retreated because the lancers' lances were longer.

phases.title: The Royalist infantry breaks in panic
phases.text: The Mounted Grenadiers ran towards Samaca. The charge of the two patriot cavalry squadrons caused panic among the infantry, which was formed in a column. It was ordered to charge with the bayonet but did not, and it broke.

phases.title: Bejar fords the river behind the Royalist vanguard
phases.text: A kilometre and a half behind Casa de Teja, Bejar's detachment managed to ford the river and approached the rear of the Royalist vanguard on the far bank.

phases.title: Santander storms the bridge
phases.text: When Bejar's detachment reached the Royalist vanguard, the two engaged. Santander led a bayonet charge across the bridge, and the Royalist vanguard fled, leaving its commander Colonel Juan Tolrá dead on the bridge.

note: The accounts give no compass directions, so the plan is laid out by the story: the patriots came from Tunja, the Spanish rearguard lay on the far side of Casa de Teja from the river, and the Spanish vanguard stood across the Teatinos River. The accounts do not say where the small hill lay beyond that it was close to Casa de Teja, or which way each Spanish part fled; the places on the plan are by judgement. The river is drawn as a straight line.
